roads.name: Vernon-Slocan Highway
words: Sweeping and steady: 64 curves in 17.7 miles.
The 4 miles at the south end are tamer.
About 3 miles in the middle are tamer.
From 1,786 to 2,860 ft, with 4,716 ft of up and down along the way.
Wooded nearly the whole way.
Water alongside for stretches.
roads.ratingNote: A full bar is top marks for that part; the percentages are each part's share of the rating. Curves, length and up and down are ranked against every road in the library. The rest are scored on the road itself: how few side roads join it, whether the curves or the limit set the pace, and how little is built up along it. At the 80 km/h limit its corners still ask for about 0.81 g, so the curves, not the limit, set the pace. Most of it has no posted limit on the map, so this takes British Columbia's 80 km/h.

roads.name: Kaslo-New Denver Highway
words: Properly twisty: 80 curves in 13.3 miles, about 6 a mile.
About 2 miles in the middle are tamer.
From 1,826 to 2,840 ft, with 1,990 ft of up and down along the way.
Wooded nearly the whole way.
16 parks, trailheads and other stops along it, so it's likely busier than most, especially on weekends.
